title: The Four Priorities Powering P&G Product Supply
summary: Building a faster, smarter and more resilient supply chain at P&G that’s ready for what’s next.
body_markdown:
## Delivering Ambition 2030 through Operational Excellence & Innovation


For P&G Product Supply, operational excellence isn’t only about making and moving products efficiently. It’s also about finding better ways to do it.


In 2021, P&G announced an ambition to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across its supply chain and operations by 2040, from raw material to retailers. To help pace our progress toward 2040, we have established near-term science-based targets for 2030 related to Scope 1 & 2 emissions, renewable electricity and transportation emissions. P&G also set a goal to reduce supply chain emissions* by 40% per unit by 2030 versus a 2020 baseline, an important milestone on the path toward net zero.


Reaching our[net zero ambitions](https://us.pg.com/blogs/climate-initiatives-net-zero-ambition/) requires innovation, cost-effective new technologies, and continued progress across our operations.


At P&G’s Budapest site, for example, the team is building a geothermal energy system designed to replace natural gas with a local, renewable resource to both heat buildings and support manufacturing processes. The project is expected to reduce the plant’s greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 90% from 2010 levels.


P&G is also looking beyond our own walls to help accelerate change across industry. A founding member of the[Renewable Thermal Collaborative](https://www.renewablethermal.org/) (RTC), a coalition working to accelerate clean industrial heat, P&G supports RTC and its work to help suppliers advance their clean heat transition.


Together, these efforts demonstrate how sustainability and operational excellence can go hand in hand.
